subject: Canary / A-B fallback & version pin request for SLO-sensitive rollout
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cleargate.ai>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cleargate.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: canary + auto-fallback plan for latency-sensitive rollout

Michael —

Thanks for jumping on this. We’re planning to flip traffic for ClearGate’s LLM feature (customer-facing autocomplete) next week. Legal and Product flagged the 99.9% p95 latency requirement in our contract and want a formal mitigation plan from Redwood that covers staged rollouts, automatic fallback, and version pinning in case of regressions.

Key asks:
- A canary + A/B plan that guarantees automatic failover to a pinned previous model if p95 latency > 420ms for more than 3m across the region.
- Clear operational thresholds and who signs off for an emergency rollback.
- A short SLA addendum we can attach to the deployment runbook.

We’d like to get your proposal and any telemetry samples by Friday so our infra team can run a dry-run.

Attaching the product acceptance checklist (referenced only).

Elena Ortiz
Director of Engineering, ClearGate
elena.ortiz@cleargate.ai

Attachments: product_acceptance_checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cleargate.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: canary + auto-fallback plan for latency-sensitive rollout

Elena —

Thanks — we can absolutely do this. High level plan below; I’ve looped in Laura (Product Ops) and Rishi/Neha (Infra) to validate thresholds and automation.

Proposed approach (summary):
1) Canary phase: 5% traffic for 30m, then 20% for 1h, then 50%/100% ramp pending health checks.
2) Telemetry gates: p95 latency, error rate, and queue depth. Automatic fallback if p95 > 420ms OR error rate > 1.5% for a sustained 3m window.
3) Pinning: if fallback occurs, we pin to last-known-good model version for 24h while we investigate; auto-retry to new version allowed only after manual sign-off.
4) Observability: we’ll provide a one-click revert in the Console and a lightweight DocuSign addendum for the carveout.

Laura — can you attach the telemetry thresholds CSV and a draft SLA addendum? Rishi/Neha — can you confirm the feasibility of the 3m sustained-window automation and that KV-caching won’t exacerbate warm-start variance?

I’ll consolidate into a short runbook for your ops team.

Thanks,
Mike
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

Attachments: none

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cleargate.ai>, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: canary + auto-fallback plan for latency-sensitive rollout

Elena / Team —

Uploading the recommended gates and a draft SLA carveout. Summary of the CSV values (attached as canary_telemetry_thresholds.csv):
- p95_latency_threshold_ms: 420
- sustained_window_seconds: 180
- error_rate_threshold_pct: 1.5
- request_queue_depth_threshold: 50
- consecutive_interval_scale_back: 2 (number of evaluation windows before scaling pin)

Pin semantics (from Product Ops):
- Immediate pin: executed automatically when a gate trips; routes all traffic to pinned version within region in <30s.
- Pin duration: 24 hours default, auto-extend only by manual request from Redwood or ClearGate.
- Canary-tagging: we tag each canary run with telemetry snapshot + commit id for audit.

Draft SLA carveout attached as draft_sla_carveout.docx. It’s intentionally terse: states that temporary carveouts for canary safety are bilateral, limited to emergency routing to prior version, and do not constitute a change to baseline SLA without explicit approval.

Operational notes:
- Rishi, Neha — we recommend enabling KV-prefix caching in read-through mode during the canary window to minimize cold-start tail latency, but we need to watch for cache warming artifacts.
- Tessa — can you schedule a short DR call during the first 20 minutes of the 20% ramp?

Laura Bennett
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: canary_telemetry_thresholds.csv, draft_sla_carveout.docx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cleargate.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: canary + auto-fallback plan for latency-sensitive rollout

Team —

I looked at the thresholds Laura proposed and the automation path. Infra can implement the 3-minute sustained-window automatic failover and immediate pin for region scope. A few clarifications and constraints:

1) Telemetry windows: we’ll evaluate three rolling 60s windows and require 3 consecutive windows above threshold to trigger pin (matches the 180s sustained window).
2) Cross-region failover: our automatic pin is regional; global failover requires manual approval because of data residency and routing complexity.
3) Warm-up artifact mitigation: to avoid false positives during the initial 5% ramp, we’ll use prefix-based warmup overrides for 10 minutes; if any gate trips during that period we’ll mark as warmup-failure and require manual review.
4) Audit & revert: all pins create an audit event and optional auto-rollback policy that will attempt a controlled retry after 4 hours if the new version has been patched and re-validated in a canary namespace.

Given the SLA sensitivity, I approve the conditional carveout subject to ClearGate ops acknowledging the warmup override.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachments: none

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cleargate.ai>, ops@cleargate.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: canary + auto-fallback plan for latency-sensitive rollout — confirmation and next steps

Elena —

Thanks again. Per Rishi/Laura we have a firm plan and the following consolidated asks before we proceed with the production flip:
- ClearGate to acknowledge the warmup override for the first 10m of the initial canary ramp (we’ll mark warmup-failures and require manual review).
- Sign the attached DocuSign addendum (link below) authorizing the 24h automatic pin behavior and the defined thresholds.
- Ops contact for first 60m DR call: ops@cleargate.ai — please confirm a pager or on-call contact.

If you confirm the three bullets we’ll schedule the run next Wednesday 07/07 and provision a canary namespace for dry-run on Monday 07/05. I’ve attached the draft SLA carveout and telemetry CSV for your records.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Sign?doc=CG-4721-SLA-Addendum
Runbook (internal): https://docs.redwood.ai/s/CG-4721-canary-plan

Mike
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

Attachments: draft_sla_carveout.docx, canary_telemetry_thresholds.csv
